title: Where does the club go?
hook: An articulated fossil can connect a feature to the body.

knows: Some fossils preserve bones in connected positions.
doesNotKnow: Use an articulated connection to locate a tail club.

misconception: An isolated-looking feature can only be assigned by guessing.
objective: Use an articulated connection to locate a tail club.

claims.text: An articulated fossil can connect a feature to the body. An identified ankylosaur fossil preserves a bony club attached to articulated tail bones. Where does the evidence place the club? The schematic shows a bony club connected to the end of the tail by articulated bones. In the stipulated fossil this connection provides evidence of position; the drawing does not establish how the club was used.

Exact supporting specimens or passages have not yet been checked.

claims.text: The figure is a simplified, not-to-scale schematic of a stated example, not an image of an identified specimen.
Recall: A fossil club is articulated with the end of a tail. Where is it placed? Its connection to tail bones places it at the tail end in the stipulated specimen.
